commitResults.messageTitle: Rename main class and add greeting
Implement add task and list task functionality
Implement mark and unmark task functionality
Implement todo, deadline, and event task types
Remove input that asks user for their name
Dates: Store deadline and event dates

commitResults.messageBody:
MrChatbot handles command flow and task changes while also printing every response directly.

Mixing console interaction code into the main class makes the next OOP extraction steps harder to review.

Extract the welcome, help, list, task mutation, error, and input-reading behavior into a Ui class so later Parser and TaskList extraction can be smaller behavior-preserving changes.

MrChatbot still owns command flow, but it also contains the rules for classifying commands, validating command arguments, and constructing task objects.

Keeping those parsing rules in the main class makes the remaining OOP extraction harder to review because behavior and orchestration are mixed together.

Move command classification, task creation, date parsing, and task-number parsing into Parser. This keeps the chatbot behavior unchanged while making the next TaskList extraction smaller.

MrChatbot should not need to know which commands accept arguments and which commands must match exactly.

Move that distinction into CommandType so command classification gives MrChatbot a cleaner enum result. This keeps inputs like list, help, and bye exact-only while preserving argument commands such as mark, unmark, and delete.

MrChatbot still manipulates the raw task collection directly for marking, unmarking, deleting, and checking capacity.

That keeps list-management details in the coordinator and makes the main loop harder to read as more behavior is added.

Introduce TaskList to own task storage, task-number validation, and task mutations. Update Ui and Storage to work with TaskList so MrChatbot can coordinate commands without direct ArrayList operations.

MrChatbot still handles every command branch directly, which keeps the main loop far from the command-object structure suggested by the stretch goal.

Start the command extraction with the safest commands: bye, help, and list. These commands do not mutate tasks or write storage, so they can move behind Command.execute without changing persistence behavior.

Let Ui remember the display name so ExitCommand can print the bye message without a special case in MrChatbot.

MrChatbot still contains the command branches for mark, unmark, and delete even though those branches all follow the command-object execution shape.

Move those branches into MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand, and DeleteCommand. Parser now creates those commands after parsing the task number, while each command owns the task mutation, save, and confirmation message.

This keeps persistence and UI behavior unchanged while making the main loop closer to executing parsed commands uniformly.

MrChatbot still handles task creation results directly after Parser returns null for add commands.

That keeps the main loop partly branch-based even though the other commands already execute through Command objects.

Introduce AddCommand to own capacity checking, adding the parsed task, saving, and showing the confirmation. Parser now returns a command for task creation inputs, so MrChatbot can execute parsed commands uniformly.

All production classes still live in the default package, which makes the growing command, parser, storage, task, UI, and exception classes harder to navigate.

Move the classes under the mrchatbot package tree while keeping src/main/java as the source root. Split CommandType into its own parser package file and add task getters so storage can access task data cleanly across package boundaries.

Update the UI test runner and README so local tests and setup instructions use the packaged main class.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tests: Add JUnit coverage for core logic
commitResults.messageBody:
Add focused JUnit tests for parser, storage, and task list behavior.

The tests cover valid and invalid command parsing, persistence edge cases, task mutation operations, and file round-tripping so regressions in the main business logic are easier to catch.

commitResults.messageTitle: Gradle: Set correct application main class
Docs: Add JavaDoc comments to source code
commitResults.messageBody:
Document public and package-private source APIs so each class and method has a clearer purpose.

The comments cover the application entry point, command execution methods, command type helpers, and task display methods.

commitResults.messageTitle: Style: Align Java code with coding standard
Docs: Add SE-EDU Java coding standard skill

commitResults.messageBody:
Configure Gradle to run Checkstyle using the SE-EDU configuration from AddressBook Level 3.

Also fix existing parser and parser-test style issues so the new checks pass immediately.

Route both the JavaFX interface and the existing CLI through a shared command engine so the text UI remains usable for testing. Add inline command guidance in the GUI input while keeping the underlying command parser unchanged.
Allow tests and setup code to create fixed task lists directly without repeated add calls. Keep the existing collection constructor for tasks loaded from storage.

Parser helpers, task display, and storage rely on internal assumptions
that are implicit. Programming mistakes can otherwise cause unclear
index errors or save an unsupported task using the Todo format.

Add Java assertions with diagnostic messages and comments explaining
each assumption. Require a complete delimiter before extracting event
values and at least one missing field before building its error message.
Check display indices against the task list bounds and require Todo
for the storage fallback after Deadline and Event are handled.

Keep user-input and saved-file validation as exceptions because these
errors must still be handled when assertions are disabled. Assertions
contain no side effects and document contracts between internal callers.

Validate with Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu and ./gradlew check. All 33 tests and
both Checkstyle checks pass.
Document internal assumptions with assertions

Task creation mixes command selection with the validation and parsing
rules for three task types in one long method. Readers must scan
unrelated branches to understand a single command's behavior.

Extract one parsing method per task type and let createTask select the
appropriate method. Keep each command's missing-field checks close to
its parsing logic while preserving existing messages and date handling.

This follows the code quality guidelines on avoiding long methods and
keeping each method at one level of abstraction. Add regression coverage
for missing fields and reversed, uppercase event delimiters to protect
the behavior while reorganizing the code.

Validate with Java 25 and ./gradlew check: all 37 tests and Checkstyle
checks pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate save steps from temporary-file cleanup
commitResults.messageBody:
Saving tasks combines line formatting, temporary-file selection,
writing, replacement, and nested cleanup handling in one method. The
failure-handling details obscure the normal save sequence.

Extract focused helpers for formatting, temporary-file creation, and
best-effort cleanup. Keep saveTasks responsible for coordinating the
save and reporting its existing error message.

This follows the guidelines on logical structure, short methods, and
making the happy path prominent. Preserve the original cleanup comment
and behavior so a cleanup failure cannot hide the useful save error.

Add a regression test that forces replacement to fail and verifies the
existing contents survive and the temporary file is removed. All 38
tests and Checkstyle checks pass with Java 25 and ./gradlew check.

The JavaFX start method mixes window setup with low-level construction
of the chat history, input controls, syntax hints, and shortcut panel.
This makes the overall screen structure difficult to see at a glance.

Extract methods for the dialog pane, input panel, and guided text input.
Keep start focused on assembling the window and starting the engine.
Make the send button local to the panel that owns it because no other
method uses it.

This follows the guidelines on short methods, a single level of
abstraction, and minimal variable scope. Preserve layout properties,
styles, event handlers, and initialization order to retain the existing
interface behavior.

Validate compilation, all 38 unit tests, and Checkstyle using Java 25
and ./gradlew check. GUI interaction is not covered by these tests.

MrChatbot contains a private toTitleCase method with no callers. The
console uses a fixed user name, so the helper has no effect on behavior
and suggests a name-input feature that is not present.

Remove the unused method and its associated documentation. This follows
the guideline to delete dead code, reducing the amount of unrelated
logic readers must understand when following console startup.

The implementation remains available in Git history if a future feature
needs it. Java 25 compilation, all 38 tests, and Checkstyle pass through
./gradlew check.
Improve code readability with focused refactors

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams for task filtering and storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Task searching and storage use loops to filter tasks, transform tasks
into saved lines, and check whether any required field is blank. These
operations can express their intent directly with Java streams.

Use filter for matching tasks, map for storage lines, and anyMatch for
blank-field detection. Preserve encounter order and collect search
results into an ArrayList to retain the existing mutable return type.

Keep parsing loops that track escape state or handle checked exceptions
unchanged, since streams would make those operations harder to follow.

Validate with Java 25.0.3.fx-zulu and ./gradlew check. All 33 tests and
both Checkstyle checks pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master into the streams branch
commitResults.messageBody:
The streams branch predates the assertions and code-quality work now
on master. Storage formatting changes overlap with the extracted helper
introduced by that work.

Merge master and resolve the overlap by keeping formatTaskLines and
implementing its task-to-line conversion with a stream. Retain the
assertions, parser and GUI refactors, and failed-save cleanup behavior.

Validate the combined changes with Java 25 and ./gradlew check. All 38
tests and both Checkstyle checks pass.
Use streams for task filtering and storage

commitResults.messageTitle: Add daily and weekly recurring tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks retain their completion status indefinitely, so users must
manually recreate or unmark activities that repeat on a schedule.

Add recurring tasks with /every day or /every week and an optional
/on weekday for weekly tasks. Default weekly schedules to the creation
weekday and choose the first reset strictly after the creation date.

Refresh recurring tasks at startup and before each command. Advance
past all missed intervals while preserving the scheduled weekday, so
completion never shifts the schedule and missed periods do not create
a backlog. Persist automatic resets and retry failed saves before
processing another command.

Store recurrence and next reset date alongside completion status while
preserving existing task records. Show the schedule and next reset in
task output, and document the syntax and local-date semantics in help
and the README.

Use an injectable clock to test boundaries without waiting. Java 25
./gradlew check passes all 54 tests and both Checkstyle checks, covering
weekday selection, missed intervals, restart persistence, malformed
records, existing commands, and failed-save retries.
Add daily and weekly recurring tasks

commitResults.messageTitle: Add chat avatars and recurring-task shortcuts
commitResults.messageBody:
Chat messages lack visual speaker identities, and the shortcut bar does
not expose the recurring-task commands supported by the engine.

Add circular robot and user portraits beside their respective messages.
Draw the portraits with JavaFX so they need no external image files.
Keep avatars aligned with the top of each message bubble.

Add daily-task and recurring-task shortcuts, select the description
placeholder for replacement, and show recurrence syntax guidance.
Allow shortcut buttons to wrap so the additional controls fit the
window. Label the weekly template button as recurring task.

Validate with Java 25: all 54 tests and Checkstyle pass. Relaunch the
application with the updated interface. The final button-label change
only changes its displayed text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject events with invalid date order
commitResults.messageBody:
Event commands accept an end date that is before or equal to the start
date. Such an event has no valid positive date range and can confuse
users reviewing their task list.

Validate the parsed dates before creating an event and report that the
end date must be after the start date, together with the command format.
Keep existing date-format validation and valid event behavior intact.

Add regression coverage for earlier and equal end dates, including
commands with the date delimiters reversed. All 55 tests and Checkstyle
checks pass with Java 25 and ./gradlew check.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge event date validation into master
commitResults.messageBody:
Integrate the reviewed error-handling improvement so event commands
reject end dates on or before their start dates with a clear message.

The feature includes regression tests for invalid date ordering and
preserves valid event parsing. All 55 tests and Checkstyle checks pass
with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Write a practical Mr Chatbot user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide contains placeholder sections and does not explain how
to use the chatbot's implemented features.

Replace the placeholders with concise startup guidance, command examples,
recurring-task behavior, and saving and troubleshooting information.
Explain task status, date restrictions, the task limit, and the need to
use full-list task numbers rather than search-result numbers.

Keep the product name prominent and use compact command tables so users
can quickly find the action they need. Check the documented behavior
against the implementation and validate whitespace with git diff --check.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use the Mr Chatbot name for the save file
commitResults.messageBody:
The default save path still uses the Duke template name, which does not
match the application's identity and can confuse users locating data.

Change the default path to data/mr-chatbot.txt and update the User Guide
to point to the same file. Keep the storage format unchanged.

Validate with Java 25 and ./gradlew check: all 55 tests and both
Checkstyle checks pass.

Project instructions do not explicitly link the course commit rules.
Future changes need a durable reference to the requested conventions.

Document the course and SE-EDU sources together with subject and body
requirements so later work follows the same commit-message standard.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain migration from the old save filename
commitResults.messageBody:
The guide names the new save file but gives existing users no way to
bring forward tasks stored under the Duke filename.

Explain how to copy the old file with the app closed, keep a backup,
and avoid overwriting an existing new file. Clarify that migration is
manual so users do not assume an empty list means their data was lost.

commitResults.messageTitle: Link the User Guide from the project README
commitResults.messageBody:
The project README focuses on setup and does not direct readers to
the complete command reference.

Add a relative link to the User Guide near the introduction so users
can find feature instructions from the repository landing page.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify how recurring shortcuts are submitted
commitResults.messageBody:
The guide mentions inserted templates but does not explicitly explain
whether clicking a shortcut submits a task.

Clarify that users must send the completed command and show how to add
a weekday to the weekly template. This makes the shortcut workflow
clear without adding another lengthy walkthrough.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename the packaged JAR to mr-chatbot.jar
commitResults.messageBody:
The packaged application still uses the Duke template filename, which
inconsistently identifies the app when users locate or launch it.

Name the Shadow JAR mr-chatbot.jar to match the product name and make
the distributable easier to recognize.

Validate with Java 25 and ./gradlew clean shadowJar. The build succeeds
and produces build/libs/mr-chatbot.jar.
